imbalance.explanation: Total Debits ({{debits}}) {{relation}} Total Credits ({{credits}}). In double-entry bookkeeping these two totals must always be equal — every posted transaction debits one account and credits another for the same amount.
imbalance.cause1: A journal entry was posted with unequal debit and credit totals (e.g. via a direct database edit, import, or migration that bypassed validation)
imbalance.cause2: An opening balance was entered for an account without a matching offsetting entry
imbalance.cause3: A posted journal entry was later edited or deleted without reversing both its debit and credit sides
imbalance.fix1: Open Journals and look for any entry whose debit and credit totals don't match — the New Journal Entry form blocks this, so an existing imbalanced entry usually predates that check
imbalance.fix2: Click an account row below to open its ledger and trace transactions for an unexpected closing balance
imbalance.fix3: Post a correcting journal entry for {{amount}} against a Suspense/Clearing account, then investigate and reclassify it once the source is found
imbalance.fix4: If this followed a data import or migration, re-run it ensuring every batch of entries is balanced before posting

role.customer: Customer balances (wallet, store credit, house account)

invoice.name: Sales invoices
invoice.notes: Posted when the invoice is sent (manually or by schedule); reversed on cancel or reset.

invoice-payment.name: Invoice payments
invoice-payment.notes: Posted when a payment is recorded on an invoice. Cash or bank is chosen by payment method.

receipt-voucher.name: Receipt vouchers
receipt-voucher.notes: Posted with realised exchange gain or loss; reversed on void.

purchase-bill.name: Purchase bills
purchase-bill.notes: Posted on approval; reversed on cancel. Purchases are expensed — stock is not carried in the ledger.

payment-voucher.name: Payment vouchers
payment-voucher.notes: Posted with realised exchange gain or loss; reversed on void.

expense.name: Expenses
expense.notes: Posted when paid. The expense account comes from the category unless one is chosen on the expense.

bank-transaction.name: Bank transactions
bank-transaction.notes: Bank transactions change the bank account balance only. No journal entry is raised, so the bank balance and ledger account 1010 can drift apart. They are deliberately not posted from here: a bank line has only one side (nothing says what the money was for), bank accounts are not tied to ledger accounts, and receipt and payment vouchers already post the same money, so posting both would count it twice. The way to close the gap is bank reconciliation.

sale.name: Retail POS sales
sale.notes: Each completed sale is collected once. A sale later refunded is still posted in full; the refund is posted separately. Sales paid from store credit go to the customer-balances account, not the bank.

refund.name: Retail POS refunds
refund.notes: Reverses revenue and tax for the refunded amount and credits whichever of cash, bank or store credit the refund was paid back through.

order.name: Restaurant orders
order.notes: Collected when the order reaches paid. Tips are held as a liability, not revenue. Wallet and house-account payments go to the customer-balances account, not the bank.

refund.name: Restaurant refunds
refund.trigger: Refund recorded on a paid order
refund.notes: Posted against revenue for the refunded amount. Tax is not split out — a refund row stores one amount.

rent.name: Rent received
rent.notes: Collected when an installment is settled. Part payments are posted once the installment is paid in full.

fine.name: Library fines collected
fine.notes: Each amount taken against a fine is collected once, part payments included. Waived fines are not posted. A payment posted here is marked in the library, so its own fines posting screen cannot enter it again — and the reverse.

payroll.name: Payroll
payroll.notes: Collects approved runs that have no journal entry yet — the browser-side posting at approval silently skips when it cannot find salary accounts by name. Once posted here the entry is linked back to the run.

production.name: Production cost
production.notes: A user posts a draft journal entry from the order drawer. Completed orders with no entry are counted here.

invoice.name: Visa case invoices
invoice.notes: A draft invoice is created through the Finance API when the box is ticked. It reaches the ledger only when someone sends it.

quotation.name: Quotation to invoice
quotation.notes: A user creates a Finance invoice from the quotation. Sales orders and delivery challans post nothing.

return.name: Sales returns
return.notes: An approved return records a refund amount but raises no credit note or journal entry.

grn.name: Goods receipts and purchase returns
grn.notes: Receipts and returns update the purchase order only. The ledger expenses purchases when the bill is approved, so posting receipts as stock would double-count until bills are changed to clear an accrual account.

movement.name: Stock adjustments and write-offs
movement.trigger: Stock adjusted, written off or transferred
movement.notes: Stock value is not carried in the ledger (purchases are expensed), so there is no inventory account to adjust.

booking.name: Hotel bookings
booking.notes: A booking stores a running paid amount, not individual payments, so there is no event to post.

project.name: Construction contracts
project.notes: The module raises no journal entries.

hub.title: Finance Posting
